title: Structured response contract audit and graceful tool termination - acceptance criteria
creator: Leah Park
description: PRD-level acceptance criteria for validating structured responses (JSON/envelope frames) combined with tool/function invocation behavior. This ticket defines the matrix of allowed schema states, streaming partials, and explicit operator-visible error/fallthrough modes when a tool call is requested by the model. The goal is to provide a deterministic contract that runtime, gateway, and SDK layers can validate against during canary and release testing. This doc focuses on: (1) how to detect and classify structured-emission deviations; (2) controlled termination semantics for tool calls (client, runtime, tool proxy initiated); (3) retry and idempotency expectations; (4) observability events and test cases for streaming/slow-consumer scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Schema validation: The runtime must validate that top-level envelope keys match the agreed contract ("envelope", "type", "payload") and produce a deterministic error code (STRUCT-100) when a required top-level key is missing.

Partial/fragment emissions: For streaming responses that emit partial payloads, the system must deliver 'checkpoint' frames that include a deterministic fragment sequence id and checksum. If a stream closes without a final commit frame, the runtime must mark the emission state as 'partial' and emit an actionable operator event with code STREAM-201.

Tool invocation handshake: Before forwarding a function/tool invocation to any external tool, the gateway must perform a handshake that includes (a) tool_id, (b) schema version, (c) invocation_id. If handshake fails, the system must return a standardized failure envelope with code TOOL-HS-300 and no PII in logs.

Graceful tool termination: If an external tool returns a terminal error or is force-killed while a structured emission is in-flight, the runtime must (a) attempt retry per configured policy, (b) if retries exhausted, emit a 'tool-terminated' envelope with error classification (transient|permanent|rate-limit) and guidance for consumer clients on whether the partial payload is safe to use.

Idempotency guarantees: Tool invocations are considered idempotent only when an idempotency key is supplied by the caller. Acceptance tests will assert that repeated invocations with the same invocation_id are not forwarded to the tool more than once under normal retry flows.

Fallback model variant: When the selected model variant fails schema enforcement repeatedly (>=3 occurrences in 1 minute for same prompt set), automated routing must fall back to the compatible variant and record a rollback event with tag 'schema-fallback'. Acceptance requires validated rollback in staging.

Backpressure and slow consumer: When downstream consumers apply backpressure (TCP write backpressure, closed SSE connection), runtime must queue up to N frames or drop non-critical telemetry frames first; critical commit frames must be persisted. Tests will simulate slow consumer and assert no silent data loss for committed frames.

Observability: Each deviation must create a trace span and an event containing keys: service, invocation_id, error_code, schema_version, model_variant, region. Events must be ingested into the Console and surfaced in a per-route anomaly view within 5 minutes in staging.

End-to-end test matrix: Create automated E2E tests covering (a) well-formed streaming with tool success, (b) malformed schema with detection and failfast, (c) tool transient error with retry policy exercised, (d) tool permanent error with graceful termination and client guidance. All tests must pass in CI against the canary runtime before merging.
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2025-02-11: Use an envelope wrapper for all structured responses to simplify validation at gateways and reverse-proxies (agrees with infra preference).
Decision 2025-02-13: Idempotency will be opt-in via invocation_id; team will not mandate idempotency keys for legacy callers to avoid breaking traffic.

Trade-off: Stronger validation increases false-positives for model outputs; we've chosen to classify 'schema deviations' separately from 'semantic failures' so we can apply automatic fallbacks without alert fatigue.
Implementation note: Runtime team recommends emitting 'partial' state with a deterministic checksum (sha256 hex) of last committed frame for easy reconcilers to verify fragments.
Follow-up: Create a lightweight SDK helper to attach invocation_id and map tool error codes into user-friendly messages.

testing_checklist: Unit tests for envelope validator (schema negative and positive cases)
Integration test: handshake + tool proxy in staging with mock tool returning 500 and 429
Chaos test: tool proxy terminated mid-invoke and assertion on emitted 'tool-terminated' envelope
Load test: streaming with N=10000 concurrent streams and slow consumer node to validate backpressure policy
Observability test: ensure events appear in Console anomaly view within 5 minutes
